stemMd: Why could a lower alert count fail to show improved software reliability?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Reliability is identical to message volume.

options.label: C
options.textMd: A lower count always proves more failures.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Changed reporting rules can reduce messages without reducing failures.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Grouping messages necessarily prevents every interruption.

explanationMd: The same underlying events may generate fewer notifications under new grouping rules. Therefore the count is partly a property of the reporting system. Service interruptions and recovery provide separate evidence about reliability.

distractorRationale.c: The passage supports neither direction from count alone.
distractorRationale.e: Grouping changes reporting rather than directly repairing software.
distractorRationale.b: The team explicitly separates the measures.
distractorRationale.a: The team tracks it as a reliability-related outcome.
